children: announced the launch of its first video gaming locations in Chicago after it landed approval from the city.
Of not, the Illinois Gaming Board has approved 78 Chicago establishments for video gaming, including 25 that have partnered with Accel Entertainment
. City licenses have now been issued for eleven Accel

partner locations, with at least four locations going live this week, including Lawlor’s Bar, which is already operational. The remaining licensed locations are expected to come online by the end of 2026.

"We are proud to partner with some of the first retail establishments in the city to bring video gaming to Chicago. This opportunity will help small-business owners grow sales, reinvest in their stores, and build for the future," stated CEO Mark Phelan on the development.
The company said the launch represents a major milestone in bringing a product already embraced throughout the state to Illinois’ largest city. Accel
noted it looks forward to seeing additional partner locations receive city licenses and come online in 2027.
Weighing in on the development, Texas Capital analyst David Bain said Accel

targets ~30% share across an estimated ~2,500-location market. Bain and his team expect 100 to 200 annual activations. "We view these targets as potentially conservative given strong operator demand and ACEL's scale and state incumbency, with licensing pace as the primary gating factor," he highlighted.

title: Accel launches video gaming locations in Chicago
